translations.6b85a05e2c05ddd4cbc44bc1: Even with an official source, the data clashes: the system says one thing, the client swears another, and last week’s spreadsheet a third. The conflict rule is the sentence that explains who has authority in those cases and what to do with the discrepancy. Most important: the conflict must be recorded, not resolved in silence.
translations.8d1cc91f57836f50ea86d56c: A conflict resolved in silence becomes an invisible error: the agent picks one version, moves on, and nobody knows. When it’s recorded, the conflict becomes useful information. If the system’s inventory and the kitchen count disagree every week, the problem isn’t the agent—it’s the counting process.
translations.34e3ac4a14598cc3d756220a: Hierarchy: which source wins over which.
translations.b341c132223e9b011a7a4a6b: When in doubt: what to do if the official one seems wrong.
translations.3d483d60ee7ee0340dc06c05: Record: note the conflict in the report.
translations.1fecfa4277c5b3090f0bd46e: Correction: fix the source that was wrong.
translations.9f609dcd365f6a78935cde71: Hallucination is the name given when the AI produces false information that looks real: a time that doesn’t exist, a law nobody wrote, a guessed price. It doesn’t lie on purpose; it completes the text with what seems likely. That’s why the instruction needs an explicit rule: when something is missing, the agent must warn you and not invent.
translations.b79bb3b14e24af02cb4761ba: Invented data is the most dangerous error because it doesn’t look like an error. A guessed delivery deadline sounds as confident as a real one. Telling the agent what to do when information is missing—using a concrete action—turns the guess into a warning you can actually handle.
translations.66a0f48b5395c3582be93087: Hallucination: a false answer that looks right.
translations.c85a5d35c83f552f18ad6e3c: Trigger: a question with no data in the source.
translations.0d9fa8d9e05ab7d1bb79c2aa: Concrete action: mark as pending, ask for the data, or pass it to you.
translations.0b74bc58537646fb1a777ea4: Acceptance criteria, or definition of “ready,” is the description of what the result looks like when the work is done well. The Ficha question is “what does a day look like when this was perfect?” The answer must be observable: something you can see or count, not something you feel.
translations.343744337bd732c5f665d7bc: Without a definition of “ready,” the agent stops when it thinks it’s done—and it always thinks it is. “I confirmed the consults” could mean sending three messages. With an observable criterion, it knows when the task is truly finished, and you know what to check.
translations.83f606a14e776471cc2befe0: Result: what exists at the end, in full.
translations.c6e52360871b978695db9b98: Observable: something you can see or count.
translations.b487ac9693753bdc502bb886: Deadline: until when it needs to be ready.
translations.cc465c66a1cb6cee91d3e5b3: Exceptions: what goes to you, and doesn’t count as a failure.
translations.8cb9f4d87649589ea9401708: A metric is a number that tracks the work over time: how many messages were sent, how many people replied, how many cases came to you. The rule is to count, not to guess. A good simple metric fits in the daily report and anyone on the team can check it.
translations.9bb66b415bce6cc56dbb2234: First impressions can mislead: a day with loud complaints can seem worse than it really was. Simple numbers show trends. If the cases passed to you decrease week after week, the agent is improving; if they rise, some rule needs adjustment. And it’s with those numbers that you later decide whether it can be given more autonomy.
translations.3c4bcbfc03bbdec51d841c86: Exceptions: how much came to you.
translations.dd3499cf28029a3e0e7e1788: Errors: how much went wrong, noted without hiding.
translations.1a4c924b88cf18069c5b2253: Before running an agent, you test the three points where agents usually fail: missing information, a prohibited request, and an alarm situation. These are the same three tests that the Agent Sheet generates to prepare for each sheet. If it makes any mistake, you adjust the instruction and repeat.
translations.003a744bd45b1bcc862db905: An agent that handles normal cases well can fail badly on difficult cases—and difficult cases are the ones that cause damage. Testing first costs ten minutes. Finding out later, with a real client, costs much more: an improper refund, a made-up date, a complaint answered in the wrong tone.
translations.098faaeb23dee376aa06c337: Test 1: missing or contradictory information; it warns you and doesn’t make things up.
translations.23d23f57fd274511a7964e06: Test 2: prohibited request; it refuses and passes it to you.
translations.c096dcc789ee60b626d1dae6: Test 3: alarm situation; it stops and calls you.
translations.54204f5edab63acbff46d906: Bonus: compare a run with the definition of “ready.”
